newsitem.title: ERITREA: Eritrea eyes dormant volcano for electric power.
newsitem.headline: Eritrea eyes dormant volcano for electric power.

text.p: Geothermal energy from beneath a dormant volcano may help to power economic growth and cut expensive oil imports to impoverished Eritrea, an official said on Monday.

Samuel Baire, head of the energy department, told Reuters a study by American and Eritrean geologists had shown geothermal potential around volcanic Mount Alid, south of the Red Sea port city of Massawa.
"As a source of energy, if it becomes viable, there is an option to produce power in that area," said Samuel.
"In the long run it could save costs, even though the initial investment is very high."
Mount Alid lies on the geologically active Rift Valley which arcs from northeast to southern Africa.
Geothermal energy can be harnessed when underground water is boiled by volcanic heat into steam, which is then used drive turbines and generate electricty.
Although geothermal energy could not satisfy all Eritrea's needs it could help to reduce imports of oil, which is currently the only source of electric power. Samuel said that another
study would still need to be carried out to give a better idea of how much geothermal power could be provided, and how much it would cost to exploit.
"We need to test the temperature deep down, the recharging capacity of water, and the chemical composition of the water," Samuel said.
However the United States Agency for International Development only agreed to fund the first phase of the study.
"We have asked different organisations (for funds), but we have had no answer so far", said Samuel.
Many of Eritrea's more than 3.5 million people are not supplied with electricity at all and an estimated 90 percent of energy needs are provided through burning fuel wood and charcoal.

Government officials said between 230,000 and 250,000 tonnes of crude oil imported into Eritrea in 1996 were for its own use. Figures were unavailable for the amount of refined diesel and fuel oil used in power generation.
Eritrea may have significant offshore reserves of oil and gas, but explorations by American company Anadarko Petroleum Corp. are still at an early stage.
Eritrea gained independence from its much larger neighbour Ethiopia in 1993 after a long guerrilla war.
